thread:
Tanvi Patel: Quick heads-up — launching an entitlement scrub focused on admin-level RBAC + KMS bindings across cloud projects and the Console. Goal: 2-week sweep, aim to reduce interactive admin roles by ~40% where safe. Need owners for: KMS bindings, service-account ownership, and audit log exports. Who can take KMS?

Ben Gomez: timeline sounds fine. Question — do we explicitly exempt infra service accounts that need HSM/KMS access? mapping to owners is messy. :thinking_face:

Tanvi Patel: Good call. Plan is to tag infra SAs with label "infra=true" and treat them as low-change for this sweep. We'll still list them in the report but not remove roles. Need to identify keys where rotation_enabled=false and keys bound to broad groups.

Sara Liu: I can run a baseline snapshot tonight and post results. Here's the query I'll use for project-level roles (quick example):

```
SELECT principal, role, resource
FROM iam_bindings
WHERE role IN ('roles/owner','roles/editor','roles/compute.admin')
  AND resource_type='project'
```

Sara Liu: Also going to pull KMS IAM and export to CSV to feed into the scrub checklist. Will tag any principals that are serviceAccount:* and have no recent key usage.

OpsBot: nightly-kms-scan: Found 12 keys with broad IAM (includes group/* or allAuthenticatedUsers). 7 service accounts with no key activity in >180 days. Report URL: https://internal.re/redwood-reports/kms-scan-171900

Leo Kim: I'll take KMS bindings. Proposal: canary in two non-prod projects. For each canary, change role -> least-priv variant (e.g., roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter scoped to specific key) and monitor for 72 hours. If telemetry is clean, roll to staging, then prod. :thumbsup:

security-oncall: Add a required audit export step — copy audit logs + iam snapshots to a secure bucket (kms-protected) and set retention to 90 days. Compliance wants a pre-removal notification 48h before any admin entitlement deletion. Also record ticket IDs.

Ben Gomez: What's the rollback plan if an app breaks after role removal? We should use a short-lived policy pin that allows quick revert. Suggest we keep an automated policy snapshot and reapply within 15 minutes. Also add alerting on auth-failures spike.

Tanvi Patel: Agreed. Rollback plan: 1) reapply last IAM snapshot via infra-automation job, 2) open high-priority incident if revert fails. I'll add the automation job to the runbook.

Sara Liu: Posting the initial orphaned-SAs list and a trimmed IAM report to the channel after the job finishes at ~23:00 UTC. Will mark SAs with "infra=true" and add owner hints from git history.

Leo Kim: For KMS drift we should also check for policy bindings that reference groups (egrdx-admins) — sometimes groups inherit more perms than intended. I'll produce a mapping of group -> members.

Tanvi Patel: Action items:
- KMS bindings owner: @Leo Kim — canary by Friday (3 days).
- Audit export + retention: @security-oncall — secure bucket + notification to compliance by EOD tomorrow.
- Snapshot and orphan SA report: @Sara Liu — post tonight.
- Rollback automation + alert rules: @Ben Gomez — draft runbook and alert dashboard.

Tanvi Patel: I'm creating a tracking ticket: RED-SEC-2458 (entitlement-scrub). Add any PRs or infra jobs there.

Ben Gomez: One nit — we should avoid bulk role removals in a single change. Stagger by service and use feature flags where possible.

OpsBot: deploy-policy-bot: Scheduled policy change (canary) for project redwood-nonprod-2 at 2024-05-02T03:00:00Z. Will post results to this thread after run.

Tanvi Patel: Thanks all — will follow up with the ticket checklist. Please ping if you need extra approvals. :eyes:
